Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool contingency: reservation guardrails & autoscale-exception flow

Folks —

Heads up: we’ve got a set of pilot launches and an enterprise stress test landing in the same 72-hour window starting 2027-06-30. Ops flagged that if both spiky pilots and a marketplace onboarding run concurrently, our three largest US dedicated pools could hit 95%+ utilization for short bursts. I don’t want us to scramble during the event; we need a compact contingency playbook and a defined exception flow for autoscale blocks / reservation overrides.

Can we align on two things this week:
- Guardrail definitions: what triggers an exception (util %, queue depth, SLA risk) and who approves transient reservations.
- Fast path: temporary reservation creation (30–72h), bounded preemption rules, and rollback criteria.

Attached: a quick checklist and a first-pass markdown doc with suggested guardrails. I’m proposing we allow a single-team temporary reservation up to 10% of a pool for up to 48 hours when util > 90% and SLO risk is high, with product + ops sign-off.

Please reply with concerns or edits — if nobody objects, I’ll put a short exec summary for Monday’s cadence and loop in legal for any contractual implications.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Capacity, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool contingency: reservation guardrails & autoscale-exception flow

Thanks Rishi — this is timely. A few quick reactions:

1) Trigger math: util > 90% for 10 minutes or sustained queue growth (5x normal P95) should be the operational triggers. Short spikes that self-resolve shouldn’t cause churn.

2) Approval authority: product (Laura) + oncall ops (Hannah) + capacity (Rishi) for <=48h reservations. Anything >48h or >10% of pool must go through Capacity Council (Marcus + Exec).

3) Autoscale exception: we should differentiate between "blocking autoscale" (prevent scale-out due to quota) and "policy exception" (allow higher burst). For blocking autoscale, require pre-auth — we can auto-approve if ops signals a verified incident.

I commented inline on the markdown (drive link). Happy to jump on a short sync today if helpful.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops

- Preemption rules: mark low-priority pilot workloads with tag "temp-preempt-v1" so we can evict back to normal scheduling immediately after the window.
- Communication: partner teams (Orion/Acme) must be notified 2 hours before any enforced preemption; include runbook link and expected impact matrix.
- Telemetry: add a short-lived metric (dedicated.pool.reservation_override.{pool_id}) that feeds into the ops incident channel.

Summarizing next steps and a decision request for Capacity Council:

1) Proposed short path (ops fast-path):
- Trigger: util > 90% for 10m OR queue growth 5x P95.
- Action: oncall ops can create a 24–48h temporary reservation up to 10% of a pool.
- Constraints: reservation must be tagged, preemptible, and auto-expire.
- Approvals: ops + product + capacity (Rishi) — okay for <=48h.

2) Extended exception: >48h or >10% requires Capacity Council approval. Default review SLA: 4 business hours.

3) Legal/procurement: if partner contracts are affected (marketplace deals or reserved commitments), we route to Legal — but for pilot adaptive lanes we can proceed under the ops fast-path if partners agree.

Can I get acknowledgement from Laura/Kim/Hannah that you approve this flow so I can put it on the Capacity Council deck tomorrow? If approved I’ll add a short runbook and escalation steps to the drive link and notify the Marketplace PMs (Tim Walsh at Orion Health + Acme Ops).

Thanks — Marcus
